Would You Have Paid New CLA Money for this V8-Powered Mercedes G-Class?
14 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Yeah, it’s not exactly part of the new generation Mercedes G-Wagen , but truth be told, the average Joe will likely not be able to tell the difference, at least when it comes to the exterior, because the cockpit does look old.
This machine is a 2015 model year car that is said to have had a single owner in the papers until 2026. The seller reportedly picked it up in July 2026, and after adding some 5,000 miles (8,000 km), they put it up for grabs, accepting $53,000. Is that a good deal? Well, this model usually sells from roughly $35,000 to over $60,000, and the selling price equals a brand-new CLA, as mentioned in the title.
But what model is it exactly? That would be a G 550 , meaning that it packs a V8 engine. The M273 unit that breathes air from behind the familiar-looking grille has a 5.5-liter displacement, and was good for 382 hp (387 ps/285 kW) and 391 lb-ft (530 Nm) of torque when the truck was new, enabling 0-62 mph (100 kph) in roughly six seconds. This previous generation Mercedes-Benz G-Class features a seven-speed automatic transmission, a two-speed transfer case, and four-wheel drive.
The vehicle has a black-on-black look, complemented by some chrome accents on the outside. The Exterior Stainless Steel Package is on deck, just like the Parking Package. A sport exhaust system, 18-inch wheels, a power sunroof, Designo black leather upholstery, adaptive cruise control, and a premium sound system from Harman Kardon are also included.
Photo: Cars&Bids An internal crack in the left headlight was mentioned by the owner as being a flaw, and other issues include some corrosion on the underbody components, scuffs on the cargo area sill plate, and wear on certain interior surfaces and touch points.
The A/C refrigerant was recharged, and the engine oil and filter were changed in August 2025, and more than a year before, the starter was replaced. In December 2023, when this older Mercedes G-Wagen had 61,149 miles (98,410 km), the engine oil and filter, and the brake fluid were changed, and the serpentine belt and idler puller were replaced. The thermostat was replaced in May 2022, at 48,088 miles (77,390 km), and the battery was replaced in January that same year.
At the time of cataloging, the German premium truck from the previous generation had 82,400 miles (132,600 km) on the odo. It has a clean South Carolina title, has never been involved in an accident, and has no mileage discrepancies. In addition to the vehicle, the new owner will get two keys and the tool kit, because this machine comes from a long-gone era.
If you were shopping for a previous-gen G-Wagen and came across this one listed for $53,000, would you have bought it? Those who want to see more of it can do so here on Cars&Bids.
